claims: Financial Times columnist Robert Armstrong coined "TACO" in May 2025.
"TACO" describes a market strategy where investors buy during dips caused by Donald Trump’s tariff threats, assuming he will backtrack, leading to a market rebound.
Yahoo News and NPR say the phrase "TACO" was coined to describe a pattern of behavior regarding tariff negotiations during Trump's administration.
Yahoo News and NPR say the phrase is often referred to as the "TACO trade".
Markets decline when Trump threatens steep tariffs.
Markets rise when Trump reduces or postpones them.
The New York Times and Facebook note President Trump described the question about this term as "nasty".
The New York Times and Facebook note President Trump argued his actions are "negotiation," not backing down.
Facebook and Yahoo News say "TACO" is considered a shorthand on Wall Street to describe the impact of volatile policy announcements on financial markets.
The New York Times reports that this term is distinct from the 2016 campaign phrase "taco trucks on every corner".
